business_problem: Skyrim.AI needed to deliver real-time, broadcast-quality spatial media for sports, but volumetric capture from dozens of cameras created interoperability, reconstruction, networking, and data-throughput challenges that traditional broadcast stacks could not handle efficiently.
solution_summary: Skyrim.AI built its Atlas platform as a software-defined spatial media stack on NVIDIA networking, capture, and inference technologies. Live camera data is sent directly into GPUs with GPUDirect and NVIDIA Rivermax using SMPTE 2110 low-latency transport and PTP synchronization, while NVIDIA Quantum InfiniBand, NVLink, and GPU clustering scale 3D reconstruction across distributed systems. For AI services, the company uses NIM microservices, Maxine NIM, and Instant NeRF-style workflows together with proprietary radiance-field models to reconstruct and render spatial scenes in real time. RTX 6000 Ada GPUs handle camera-to-GPU capture and current inference, while L40S and H100-class GPUs support rendering and future large-scale training. This architecture allows Atlas to deliver broadcast and in-venue experiences from the same spatial capture pipeline while keeping the platform adaptable for OTT, fantasy sports, and interactive fan experiences.

data_flow: More than two dozen 8K cameras stream synchronized data through Rivermax and GPUDirect into GPUs, reconstruction and radiance-field pipelines process the volumetric data across NVLink and InfiniBand-connected clusters, and Atlas delivers broadcast, venue, and interactive spatial outputs to downstream media experiences.
business_outcome: Skyrim.AI cut development time by a full year, lowered infrastructure costs by replacing specialized hardware with software-defined workflows, and created a platform that supports new revenue streams, richer content production, and personalized sports experiences for global audiences.

NVIDIA® Rivermax® to enhance the capture pipeline, significantly reducing development time and costs.
NVIDIA® GPUDirect® enables efficient data transfer from cameras to GPUs, bypassing the CPU.
